content:
maria: Heads up — starting ~10:10 UTC we see a spike of tiny-gpu pods Pending in us-west1. Scheduler logs show a ton of node rejects with 'insufficient devices' after nodes report thermal warnings.

maria: kubectl snippets: ```
NAME                              READY   STATUS    NODE           RESTARTS
small-job-abc-7f6cb               0/1     Pending   <none>         0
small-job-def-9b2aa               0/1     Pending   <none>         0
```

sahil: Seeing same. Nodes aren't OOMing — they're setting a taint from our thermal watchdog: gpu.thermal=hot:NoSchedule then clearing after 30s. Scheduler treats that like long-term taint and spreads pods instead of packing.

jordan: Do we have the exact taint churn pattern? Is watchdog oscillating or something upstream (driver/firmware)?

maria: Watchdog logs: ```
[10:09:58] node/gpu-node-17 thermal_warn -> taint add gpu.thermal=hot:NoSchedule
[10:10:10] node/gpu-node-17 thermal_warn -> taint remove gpu.thermal=hot:NoSchedule
[10:10:20] node/gpu-node-17 thermal_warn -> taint add gpu.thermal=hot:NoSchedule
```
It flips every ~10s on ~6 nodes. Scheduler sees repeated NoSchedule cycles and starts fragmenting allocations to avoid nodes that looked flaky.

lee: That oscillation is probably the new fan curve kernel patch we rolled yesterday. Ops bot confirmed a driver update + fan-profile change for affected instance type.

ops-bot: deploy-hook: rollback candidate v2026.03.11_fancurve available. Run rollback to test.

amit: Rolling back fan-curve for a test rack now (us-west1-rack-4). Will report in 5m.

sahil: In the meantime can we adjust scheduler toleration logic to ignore transient thermal taints <60s so we don't fragment? We already backoff on short-lived taints for allocation but looks like config doesn't handle NoSchedule adds/removes quickly.

jordan: Patch idea: treat gpu.thermal=hot as PreferNoSchedule for 60s when churn > 3 flips/min. That keeps packing but still biases away for sustained heat.

maria: Short-term manual mitigation: cordon the 6 flip-nodes and drain non-critical workloads so they stop flipping and free contiguous GPU slots. Then uncordon after rollback. Will do if rollback doesn't settle.

lee: Cost note: these flipping nodes currently sit reserved in Dedicated pools. Fragmentation is causing a ~25% drop in utilization for the pool and we start spilling to on-demand which adds ~18% unit cost for the hour. Ops needs a cleanup plan if rollback doesn't hold.

amit: rollback applied to rack-4, kernel fan pwm reverted. Temp metrics look better: fewer taint events in last 2m.

maria: Good sign. Scheduler pending count halved. Still seeing some pods stuck with NodeAffinity that prefer NVLINK nodes — those are more scarce now because of earlier spreads.

sahil: For longer-term: 1) move thermal taint handling into node health aggregator (debounce) so scheduler sees a smoothed state, 2) add a node label 'gpu.cooling-class' and prefer packing into nodes with more headroom, 3) revisit warm-pool sizing for tiny pods to absorb transient fragmentation.

jordan: Also consider descheduler policy to coalesce tiny pods every 5m when fragmentation > X%. That will proactively defragment without operator manual steps.

lee: Agree. Please put a short RFC for the debounced-taint behavior + descheduler policy. Ops wants cost numbers for the change (expected utilization uplift -> cost delta).

maria: Filing the RFC now. I'll include the rollback timeline and metrics. Thanks all — monitoring until rollback fully propagated. :eyes:
